transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-02
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Echelon DS), Liam Ortiz (Echelon Product), Priya Singh (Echelon Compliance), Noah Rivera (Echelon ML)
Shared links: bit.ly/echelon-pilot-results (scorecard), drive/redwood/echelon/prompt_sets_v3, shared:security-docs/redwood-soc2.pdf

[00:00] Jamie Ortega: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya Chen: Maya here.
[00:09] Liam Ortiz: Liam, on product.
[00:11] Priya Singh: Priya, compliance.
[00:12] Noah Rivera: Noah, ML eng.
[00:13] Sanjay Patel: Sanjay, Redwood SE.
[00:15] Jamie Ortega: cool, thanks. agenda — quick recap of last week's changes, look at the recent regression points on the scorecard, decide immediate mitigations and next artifacts.

[02:02] Maya Chen: yeah so, to summarize — after we pushed prompt-set v3 which tightened the system instructions the bot started favoring shorter, safer responses but accuracy on multi-step clinical summarization dropped about 6% on the holdout. Some examples in the spreadsheet show truncation and over-redaction.

[03:21] Sanjay Patel: mm-hmm, I looked through those. two quick hypotheses: one is the guardrail rule we added is catching legitimate corpus text as "sensitive" because of punctuation patterns — the other is a prompt framing shift that reduced chain-of-thought tokens.

[04:10] Liam Ortiz: can you unpack the guardrail bit? like is this our Redwood run-time filter or something in our eval harness?

[04:20] Sanjay Patel: it's a mix. we added a post-generation redaction layer in the pipeline and then a preflight safety check — the preflight uses substring heuristics. some of the clinical shorthand like "Pt. 59 y/o" is getting flagged as PII and then the generator is being steered to remove context, leading to lower score.

[05:00] Noah Rivera: right, and the model variant we use for the pilot is the quantized 'redwood-lite-8q' — which is slightly less tolerant to longer context because of kv cache behavior, so when you combine shorter chains plus redaction you lose the linking sentences.

[05:40] Priya Singh: from compliance, our concern is ensuring we don't accidentally leak identifiers. but we also need fidelity. are there tokens we can scrub at logging time rather than at generation time?

[06:10] Sanjay Patel: yes, two standard patterns: (1) keep redaction as a post-hoc step on the return path (logging removes PII) and (2) soft-fail guardrails where we mark the generation as 'maybe-sensitive' and route to a fallback variant that emits placeholders rather than outright truncation. the soft-fail lets the model attempt full output and then we apply more targeted redaction.

[07:05] Maya Chen: we ran an A/B with fallback last night and results were mixed — fewer truncations but some hallucinated placeholders. scorecard's 'content-fidelity' metric improved for narratives but 'entity recall' dipped in a couple categories.

[07:50] Jamie Ortega: do we have examples? maybe share two or three canonical failures?

[08:00] Maya Chen: yes — examples 17, 23 in the sheet. 17 shows the model omits medication dose after redaction; 23 shows the summary replaced a lab value with [REDACTED] even though it's not PHI under our policy.

[09:03] Sanjay Patel: that sounds like the substring heuristic being too broad — e.g., 'mg/dL' patterns triggered. quick fix is to narrow the regex to recognized PHI patterns and move ambiguous matches into the soft-fail path.

[10:12] Liam Ortiz: what about prompt framing? you mentioned we tightened instructions. can loosening solve it without increasing risk?

[10:25] Sanjay Patel: loosening helps chain-of-thought and encourages longer outputs. the tradeoff is explicit: cost/latency up, maybe a few more tokens to redact. but Redwood Optimize has an autosuggest for token-efficient phrasing — we can propose revised instruction lines that preserve context.

[11:05] Noah Rivera: also important: the 'redwood-lite-8q' kernel selection does causal attention differently. if we move to a slightly larger variant or change the compilation flags we can keep kv cache longer and reduce truncation artifacts. that's a capacity question though.

[12:00] Priya Singh: for auditability we need to see original and redacted outputs with timestamps and redaction rationale — is that something Redwood logs out-of-the-box?

[12:20] Sanjay Patel: yes — we can enable the detailed audit logs in the console. they include token-level redaction markers and the rule id that triggered it. note: enabling verbose logging increases storage and needs retention policy alignment, but you can ship logs to your KMS-backed S3 or to your Splunk instance.

[13:10] Maya Chen: sounds good. another item: the scorecard shows a regression on 'follow-up action extraction' — the model sometimes misses next steps when the note is highly unstructured.

[13:45] Jamie Ortega: is that primarily prompt or model?

[13:50] Noah Rivera: mixture — a lot of our parsers rely on clear separators. v3 removed the explicit 'Action Items:' anchor from the system instruction to encourage natural prose; that increased variability. reintroducing a light anchor in the prompt could help.

[15:00] Sanjay Patel: suggested plan: (A) revert the 'Action Items' anchor for two variants and run a diff, (B) tighten redaction regex and flip ambiguous cases to soft-fail, (C) run a dedicated throughput run on the dedicated pool to confirm latency impact.

[16:20] Liam Ortiz: how long for the artifacts? like if we get the prompt variants, how quickly can we evaluate?

[16:35] Sanjay Patel: Redwood can push a new prompt set to the pilot within 24 hours; eval turnaround depends on how many samples you want. if you give us 200 edge-case prompts, we can run them against three variants and have initial scores back in 48 hours.

[17:20] Maya Chen: we can assemble 200 by end of day Thursday.

[17:30] Priya Singh: I'm okay with soft-fail as long as we have deterministic redaction in the logs and an approvals flow for flagged items. we need RBAC on download of raw outputs.

[18:05] Sanjay Patel: yes, console supports RBAC and audit-trail for log downloads. we'll add an item for the security policy export.

[19:00] Jamie Ortega: quick question on cost — if we route ambiguous cases to fallback variant, what's the per-token delta?

[19:10] Sanjay Patel: depends on variant. fallback variant is the 16b float16 instance — rough delta was +30% token cost in our estimate. we'll send an updated burn estimate.

[20:00] Noah Rivera: can we do smart routing only for cases where the confidence score is below X? what's the confidence metric?

[20:12] Sanjay Patel: yep, we can use our built-in quality score — it's a composite of token-level perplexity and a small classifier we run post-gen. thresholding is configurable; routing rules can be policy-driven so only enterprise tiers or pilot routes use fallback.

[21:00] Maya Chen: another regression item: the prompt tuning that favored brevity also lowered explanation depth — clinicians prefer concise but not shallow. can we propose a new temperature and max-tokens?

[21:30] Sanjay Patel: propose: temp 0.2 -> 0.3 and max tokens +25%. little bump but yields better narrative cohesion. Redwood Optimize suggests these parameters for similar clinical summarization workloads.

[22:40] Liam Ortiz: let's track three KPIs this week: content-fidelity, entity-recall, and redact-precision. can we get automated charts for those in the console?

[22:52] Sanjay Patel: yes, we'll add dashboard tiles and link the scorecard.

[24:00] Jamie Ortega: any legal/procurement blockers? Priya?

[24:10] Priya Singh: on compliance, the SOC2 doc you shared looks fine but we need an exported policy that shows retention, KMS usage, and subprocessing. also a statement about on-prem handling if we scale private.

[25:05] Jamie Ortega: we'll escalate that to the Redwood security team and deliver an addendum.

[26:00] Maya Chen: quick note — we noticed a cluster of false positives tied to shorthand 'DOB:' and 'DOB' without colon. regex tuning should catch both.

[26:22] Sanjay Patel: good call — will adjust patterns.

[27:10] Noah Rivera: about the throughput run: we want logs that include tail-latency percentiles and token-cost breakdown by model. is that standard?

[27:30] Sanjay Patel: yes, we can produce p50/p95/p99 and per-model token cost. we'll also include the KV cache hit-rate metric to show if quantization is causing misses.

[29:00] Liam Ortiz: timeline recap?

[29:05] Jamie Ortega: ok — artifacts: Echelon provides 200 edge prompts by 2025-09-04; Redwood to deliver prompt variants + updated guardrail regex by 2025-09-05 and run A/B with initial metrics by 2025-09-07; throughput run logs by Noah's team 2025-09-09.

[30:20] Priya Singh: I need the export of RBAC roles and log retention policy to review — can you include that in the September 3 note?

[30:35] Jamie Ortega: yes, will include.

[31:00] Maya Chen: a small thing — some transcriptions in the sheet use 'K V cash' instead of 'KV cache' — minor but confusing for reviewers.

[31:12] Sanjay Patel: ha yeah transcription artifacts. we'll correct the sheet.

[32:00] Jamie Ortega: any other risks or open questions?

[32:10] Liam Ortiz: only one — if we move to private deployment later, will these guardrail logs and RBAC settings map over cleanly?

[32:25] Sanjay Patel: yes, the private control plane preserves the same config model; you'll just host the logs in your VPC. there are a few connector changes but no behavior change.

[33:40] Noah Rivera: can you also tag the exact model hashes in the logs so we can reproduce?

[33:46] Sanjay Patel: absolutely, model version + compilation flags are part of the trace.

[35:00] Jamie Ortega: ok final recap and next steps — we'll follow up with a short note and the links. any objections?

[35:10] Maya Chen: none.

[35:12] Liam Ortiz: good.

[35:20] Priya Singh: fine.

[35:30] Jamie Ortega: thanks everyone, we'll reconvene in the same slot next week unless we need a mid-week quick sync.

[36:00] Meeting ended.

Notes: minor transcription artifacts present (speaker overlaps, wrong casing). See action items and shared links above.
